title: A live signal that stopped working

claim.signal: dealer-gamma sign as a predictor of an intraday rule's daily win/loss
claim.claimed_effect: the gamma reading discriminates winning from losing days
claim.source: deployed feature from a separate intraday-momentum study
claim.data_needs: daily prediction stream (score, label) + a published adoption series

protocol.replication_anchor: re-derive the original study's rolling discrimination series
protocol.kill_criteria_for_the_claim: discrimination falling to or below chance out of sample, and failing to replicate on a second instrument

verdict.outcome: DECAYED AND PARTLY RECOVERED — discrimination 0.597 baseline -> 0.442 trough (below chance) -> 0.548; detectable 2.8 years before the trough; the obvious cause is eliminated, the true one remains unknown
verdict.replication: re-derivation matches the original rolling series on 551/551 windows (corr 1.000000, max abs diff 2e-16)

diagnostics.detection: CUSUM alarm 2020-07-30 at AUC 0.548 vs baseline 0.597, 1028 days before the trough
diagnostics.attribution: full-sample Spearman -0.72 flips to +0.76 after 2022; erosion began at 19% adoption -> coincides, does not explain

honest_limitations: weak signal throughout; bootstrap bands brush chance ([0.515, 0.603] in the strongest phase)
phase samples are small (121 and 134 observations)
the adoption series is annual and interpolated to daily; adequate for an overlay only
rank correlation between two trending series is inflated by the trend — the split, not the level, is the test
eliminating one cause is not identifying the true one; what changed is unknown
detector parameters come from the original study and were not pre-registered before it saw the data
